findings.issue: contradicts task clause P12.4 'record the owner's rubric scores' and the phase desiredOutcome 'the owner's judgement of the maps': every rubric cell in evidence/benchmark/summary.json carries scoredBy 'orchestrator, provisional' (the orchestrating session that ran the plugin under test scored all 12 maps), and BENCHMARK.md:35 and :125 say the owner 'confirms or replaces them at sign-off'. PROTOCOL.md:101 and rubric.md still state the score is 'given by the owner after reading each artifact', so the protocol contradicts its own Runs section. The top-level README sentence (README.md:128-130) and the evals README advertise 'a rubric score' without saying it is provisional, and the roadmap Benchmark item and the CHANGELOG line close the item as done.
findings.resolution: Have the owner score the 12 maps and replace the rubric blocks (and scoredBy) in summary.json; regenerate the BENCHMARK.md rubric cells (b21 then follows), drop the provisional caveats, or - if the owner cannot score yet - leave the roadmap item and the CHANGELOG line open and say 'provisional' in the README sentence. Align PROTOCOL.md:101 with whichever is true.

findings.issue: The Runs section describes a private repository's own Claude Code setup: a .claude/settings.json with hooks, an enabled plugin whose write guard was in deny mode, and a .claude/audit.config.json removed from the clone. That is environment-specific detail about a private repository (which tooling it runs) in a public tracked file. No denylist term, name or path is present (scan clean, 14 terms), so this is a tightening, not a leak.
findings.resolution: Generalise to 'the repository carries its own Claude Code project configuration whose write guard blocked two tools; run 2 used fresh clones without that configuration' and drop the file names and the plugin description.

findings.issue: The expectation pass counts (and the 'file references failed, 24 of 28' notes) come from 'the harness', but no grader is tracked: PROTOCOL.md:39-49 also sends the reader to 'the harness script' for the headless flags, and the only tracked check on these cells is b21 comparing the page to summary.json, which is itself unverifiable. A third party can re-run the method but not the grading.
findings.resolution: State in PROTOCOL.md and BENCHMARK.md that the grader and the key-component checklists are private and the expectation results are the owner's records, or track a repo-free grader for the three mechanical checks (flows count, file references exist, artifact under docs/architecture).

findings.issue: An Agent or Task call with no subagent_type is now labelled by its free-text description, trimmed but unbounded. The label lands verbatim in the tracked evidence profiles and the text report, so a description that quotes repository content would put it in a public file, and a description equal to 'orchestrator' would merge into the orchestrator row. This phase's 13 profiles are clean (labels are archmap:* names and Explore), so it is a latent risk of the new fallback.
findings.resolution: Cap the fallback label (for example 60 characters, newlines collapsed) and prefix or reject the reserved label 'orchestrator'; add a case to c20.
